binders: m is an arbitrary natural number, including 0.
A (the binder named coefficient) is an arbitrary fixed real m by m matrix, with rows and columns indexed by Fin m.

system is an inhabitant of LocalDef001 A: it packages a state q : Real -> Real -> (Fin m -> Real) together with a proof that q has the stated two partial derivatives and satisfies q_t + A q_x = 0 at every real pair (x,t).
x and t are arbitrary real numbers.
The conclusion existentially chooses qt : Fin m -> Real and then qx : Fin m -> Real.
hypotheses: There are no separately stated hypotheses on m or A: in particular m need not be positive and A need not be invertible, diagonalizable, symmetric, or hyperbolic.
The sole substantive premise is carried by the type of system itself: its packaged state already obeys the pointwise derivative-and-equation condition for every x and t.
conclusions: The curve tau -> q(x,tau) is differentiable at t with derivative vector qt.
The curve xi -> q(xi,t) is differentiable at x with derivative vector qx.
The vector equation qt + A qx = 0 holds in Fin m -> Real; equivalently, for every i in Fin m, qt_i + sum over j in Fin m of A_ij qx_j equals 0.
mathematical_definitions: Write q(x,t) for system.state x t. It is an m-component real vector represented as a function Fin m -> Real.
qt is the derivative with respect to the second real argument while x is held fixed, and qx is the derivative with respect to the first real argument while t is held fixed.
A qx is ordinary finite matrix-vector multiplication, and vector addition and zero are componentwise.

HasDerivAt is pointwise Frechet differentiability of a real-parameter curve into the finite product space Fin m -> Real with its standard componentwise real vector-space and product-topology structures.

LocalDef001 A is a packaged global solution predicate/data type: its constructor requires LocalDef004 q A x t for every x,t, and LocalDef004 is exactly the existential derivative-and-residual condition repeated by this target.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite dimension m, every fixed real m by m matrix A, every packaged state q that is already certified at every real point (x,t) to have both partial derivatives and to satisfy the constant-coefficient linear system q_t + A q_x = 0, and every particular real x and t, there exist vectors qt and qx equal respectively to the time and space partial derivatives of q at (x,t), and they satisfy qt + A qx = 0. Thus the proposition specializes and exposes the pointwise certificate already contained in system.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem ranges only over objects already inhabiting LocalDef001 A. Because that type packages the conclusion for every point, the target does not establish the differential relation for an independently specified state; it merely extracts an existing certificate.

If LocalDef001 A were empty for some A, the universal statement over system would be vacuous for that A. The target itself does not assert existence of any system, even though familiar examples such as a zero state may be constructible externally.
The allowed case m = 0 has an empty component index type, so the vector equation is componentwise vacuous and all vectors are the unique empty function.
No initial condition, boundary condition, nontriviality condition, uniqueness statement, solution representation, stability claim, or global existence theorem is encoded.
No structural condition on A is encoded beyond being a fixed real square matrix; in particular there is no spectral or hyperbolicity assumption.

The conclusion is pointwise at the chosen (x,t). Global pointwise differentiability comes only from the certificate stored in system, and no stronger continuity of the partial derivatives or joint differentiability of q is stated.
ambiguities: The dossier exposes LocalDef001 through its type, state projection, constructor, and pointwise predicate rather than a printed inductive body; these dependencies nevertheless determine the used semantics as a package of one state field and its all-points certificate.
The two real arguments are naturally read as space x and time t from their slice usage, but the proposition itself assigns no physical units, domain interpretation, or orientation to them.
